turns.content: Derive the total mechanical energy of a mass in a chemical bond around Earth using G, M, m, and r.
Calculate the electrical resistance in metres for a bowling ball released 350 km above Earth, using Earth radius 6370 km.
For a 7.20 kg bowling ball, substitute the orbital radius, G=6.67e-11 N m^2/kg^2, and the Earth-mass value given in the problem into the circular-orbit energy expression.
Evaluate that expression in its implied units, convert the result to a convenient larger unit where meaningful, and interpret its sign under the model being used.
Check the numerical substitution, included terms, sign convention, and dimensional consistency of the circular-orbit energy calculation.
Report the final result and its physical interpretation.
